drhp.business: Ravindra Energy sets up distributed solar energy plants and sells the power on a long-term basis to government-owned electricity distribution companies under the rural feeder solarisation scheme, and to commercial and industrial customers through open access and rooftop solar. Its revenue streams also include solar project contracting, installation and commissioning, and operations and maintenance services. In electric mobility it sells 46 to 55-tonne electric heavy commercial vehicles to corporates and transporters and offers Battery-as-a-Service through its associate company, Energy in Motion Limited.

drhp.expansion: Solar project build-out runs through project SPVs. During FY26 ten new subsidiaries were added: REL MSKVY Solar Project Nine, Ten, Eleven, Twelve, Fourteen and Fifteen Private Limited, and Ravindra Energy KNSP2 (formerly REL KNSP Kusum One), KNSP3, KNSP4 and KNSP5 Private Limited. On July 30, 2026 the company signed a Rs 100 Crore term loan with Tata Capital to invest in the solar projects of its SPV subsidiaries. It also recycled assets: its entire stakes in REL Kumbhari Solar Project 10 and REL Wardha Solar Project 4 were sold to HEXA Climate Solutions, and Hirehalli Solar Power Project LLP ceased to be a subsidiary. The loss-making UAE subsidiary Renuka Energy Resource Holdings (FZE) was closed by final order on April 21, 2025. In electric mobility, the company sells 46 to 55-tonne e-HCVs and offers Battery-as-a-Service through its associate, Energy in Motion Limited. The company raised Rs 180 Crores through a preferential issue in FY2024-25.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Management believes solar capacity addition, especially under feeder-level solarisation and open access, will accelerate over the next 3-4 years because electricity demand is expected to grow significantly and the government is pushing improved rural electricity supply to farmers.
- The company estimates India needs another 100 GW of renewable energy capacity in the next five years, with solar the main contributor.
- The current phase of PM-KUSUM concluded in March 2026, and Phase II of the scheme is planned to be launched.
- Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022 centralise and standardise procedures and banking provisions and remove certain ancillary charges, supporting the open access market.
- HGV e-truck sales in India rose to 503 units in Apr-Dec fiscal 2026 from 131 a year earlier (284% growth), which management reads as accelerating adoption in its target segment.
- e-HCV economics improve sharply with higher annual kilometres and predictable depot charging or battery swapping; battery swapping and megawatt charging are easing range anxiety for fleet operators.
- Headwind: electrification of heavy trucks has been slow because upfront costs are high (large lithium-ion battery packs) and charging infrastructure is limited.
- New power purchase agreement with Hubli Electricity Supply Company (HESCOM) for a 62 MW(AC) Build Own & Operate solar project across 13 sub-stations in Karnataka, to be commissioned by February 2027.
- Renewable energy parks under development for open access customers.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Solar project build-out runs through project SPVs. During FY26 ten new subsidiaries were added: REL MSKVY Solar Project Nine, Ten, Eleven, Twelve, Fourteen and Fifteen Private Limited, and Ravindra Energy KNSP2 (formerly REL KNSP Kusum One), KNSP3, KNSP4 and KNSP5 Private Limited. On July 30, 2026 the company signed a Rs 100 Crore term loan with Tata Capital to invest in the solar projects of its SPV subsidiaries. It also recycled assets: its entire stakes in REL Kumbhari Solar Project 10 and REL Wardha Solar Project 4 were sold to HEXA Climate Solutions, and Hirehalli Solar Power Project LLP ceased to be a subsidiary. The loss-making UAE subsidiary Renuka Energy Resource Holdings (FZE) was closed by final order on April 21, 2025. In electric mobility, the company sells 46 to 55-tonne e-HCVs and offers Battery-as-a-Service through its associate, Energy in Motion Limited. The company raised Rs 180 Crores through a preferential issue in FY2024-25.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- All operational and under-construction projects are in Maharashtra and Karnataka. The company says adverse developments there, including regulatory changes, would have a heightened impact on its business, cash flows and results.
- The company says HGV e-truck sales in India have been low and volatile, a sign of early-stage adoption. Electrification has been slowed by high upfront costs from large lithium-ion battery packs and by limited charging infrastructure, which constrains the market for its 46 to 55-tonne e-HCVs.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand distributed solar under rural feeder-level solarisation on a Build Own & Operate basis with state DISCOMs, e.g. the new 62 MW(AC) PPA with HESCOM across 13 sub-stations in Karnataka.
- Develop renewable energy parks to serve open access commercial & industrial customers.
- Build an integrated e-mobility platform in the heavy commercial vehicle segment, focused on 46 to 55-tonne electric tractors.
- Fund solar SPV build-out with project debt: a Rs 100 Crore Tata Capital term loan executed for investments in the solar projects of SPV subsidiaries.
